name: Valencia
tagline: Paella, futuristic architecture and a city beach
summary: Spain's third city combines a well-kept old town, the white buildings of the City of Arts and Sciences and a long beach, all linked by a park in the old riverbed. It is also the home of paella.
seasonNote: Las Fallas in mid-March fills the streets with giant figures and fireworks, and hotel prices triple; August is humid.
arrival: High-speed trains from Madrid take 1 hour 45 minutes, from Barcelona about 3 hours. Metro lines 3 and 5 reach the airport in 20 minutes.
gettingAround: The old town is walkable; cycle the Turia park; metro and tram to the beach.
foodTip: Real paella valenciana has rabbit, chicken and beans; eat it at lunch, not dinner. Try horchata with fartons and arroz negro.
buyTip: Lladró porcelain, fans and ceramics from Manises; saffron and rice from the Central Market.
baseArea: Ciutat Vella (old town) or Ruzafa for restaurants

items.expect: The outside is free; each building has its own ticket.
